# GAMbit Release Notes

- **GAM key and executable protection:** GAMbit now checks access permissions on GAM’s key files and who can modify `gam.exe`. It also flags configuration folders stored in OneDrive or on network shares. Checks run at startup and daily, with a one-time alert and findings displayed on **Home** and in the weekly digest. Permission checks support all Windows languages.

- **One-click permission lockdown:** Added **Settings & Updates → GAM location → Lock down GAM’s keys…** to restrict key access to your Windows account, Administrators, and SYSTEM, while allowing other users to run—but not modify—GAM. Administrator rights are requested only when needed. **After lockdown, each technician needs their own GAM configuration to use it from a separate Windows account.**

- **Restore an entire group:** Added **Account time machine → Put a whole group back**. Nightly snapshots now capture complete group membership, including external addresses and nested groups. Choose a group and date, review membership and role changes, and submit the restoration through **Approvals**. Removing members added after the snapshot is optional and off by default. Older snapshots include only your district’s accounts.

- **Warn before suspending inactive accounts:** Added **Warn first** to the **Suspend accounts nobody has signed in to** clean-up rule. Send advance email notices to affected users, optionally including their directory manager and an HR or principal mailing list. Customize the message, contact person, and notice period. Users who sign in during that period are automatically removed from the list; only those still inactive proceed to **Approvals**. Dry run sends no notices and saves no changes.
